additions.reason: The primary subject of the Torah. Yom Tov IS CALLED רגל and IS CALLED מועד — it is the hub node of Package 1 with degree 2. The Rebbe's entire argument pivots on this bechina identity: because Yom Tov IS called רגל (foot), damaging Yom Tov joy makes one's foot slip.
additions.source_quote: כִּי יוֹם טוֹב נִקְרָא רֶגֶל, וְגַם נִקְרָא מוֹעֵד

additions.reason: Yom Tov IS CALLED רגל — explicit niqra bechina. This is a dual-meaning node: רגל means both 'foot' (the literal body part whose slipping is described) and 'pilgrimage festival' (one of the three רגלים). The whole Torah's wordplay depends on this bechina identity being real.

Yom Tov IS CALLED מועד — explicit niqra bechina. Like רגל, this creates a wordplay identity: מועד means 'appointed time' (the holy festival) but also underlies מועדה as in 'רגלו מועדה' (his foot slips/stumbles). The damage to שמחת יום טוב thus 'becomes' a מועד רגל — a stumbling foot.
additions.source_quote: וְגַם נִקְרָא מוֹעֵד, וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁפָּגַם בְּשִׂמְחַת יוֹם טוֹב, נַעֲשֶׂה מִזֶּה רֶגֶל מוֹעֵד

additions.reason: Yom Tov joy is the specific aspect of Yom Tov whose damage causes the fall. It is a bechina of יום טוב itself — the joy IS the festival, since the essence of Yom Tov is simcha. The Rebbe speaks of 'פגם בשמחת יום טוב' (damage to Yom Tov joy) as the root cause, treating שמחת יום טוב and יום טוב as interchangeable. This node should be added to Package 1.
additions.source_quote: זֶה בָּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁפָּגַם בְּשִׂמְחַת יוֹם טוֹב

additions.reason: The world's laughter at the fallen person IS a bechina of the fallen joys — explicit 'הוא בחינת' statement. The שחוק is not merely caused by the fallen joys; it IS the fallen joy-sparks manifesting in this degraded form.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה הַשְּׂחוֹק שֶׁשּׂוֹחֲקִין, הוּא בְּחִינַת הַשְּׂמָחוֹת נְפוּלוֹת מִפְּגַם שִׂמְחַת יוֹם טוֹב

additions.reason: The fallen joys are explicitly stated to be the bechina of the world's laughter. They represent the Yom Tov joy-energy that fell from its holy vessel due to the sin of negligence toward Yom Tov joy. This is a key mystical concept: damaged mitzvah-joy does not disappear but falls into lower realms where it becomes the energy of mockery.
additions.source_quote: הוּא בְּחִינַת הַשְּׂמָחוֹת נְפוּלוֹת מִפְּגַם שִׂמְחַת יוֹם טוֹב

additions.reason: Idol worship is the hub of Package 3: it IS called בשת (Hosea 9 — explicit niqra bechina) AND disgracing the Moadim is equivalent to it (kAilu = as if). The Rebbe uses עכו"ם / עבודת אלילים as the conceptual anchor of the shame-sin axis.
additions.source_quote: כִּי עֲבוֹדַת אֱלִילִים נִקְרָא בֹּשֶׁת (הושע ט), וְהַמְבַזֶּה אֶת הַמּוֹעֲדוֹת כְּאִלּוּ עוֹבֵד עַכּוּ"ם (פסחים קיח)

additions.reason: Idol worship IS CALLED בשת — explicit niqra. The shame/embarrassment that comes upon the person who falls is not merely a consequence of the sin; it IS the essence of idolatry (which is בשת). This bechina is sourced to Hosea 9.
additions.source_quote: כִּי עֲבוֹדַת אֱלִילִים נִקְרָא בֹּשֶׁת (הושע ט), עַל כֵּן בָּאָה עָלָיו בּוּשָׁה

additions.reason: Disgracing the Moadim is functionally identical to idolatry — this is the halakhic-mystical equivalence sourced to Pesachim 118. The Rebbe uses this to close the circuit: the person who damaged שמחת יום טוב is in the category of one who 'disgraces the Moadim' which IS idolatry which IS shame.
additions.source_quote: וְהַמְבַזֶּה אֶת הַמּוֹעֲדוֹת כְּאִלּוּ עוֹבֵד עַכּוּ"ם

additions.reason: Note: בושה (embarrassment) is the result state of the person who fell. While closely related to בשת (Package 3), בושה here may deserve its own consideration. However, in the Torah's logic, בושה is the manifestation of בשת upon the person — 'עַל כֵּן בָּאָה עָלָיו בּוּשָׁה' — making it essentially the same node as בשת (shame) at a different description level. It should likely be an alias of בשת in Package 3 rather than a new node.
additions.source_quote: עַל כֵּן מִתְבַּיֵּשׁ... עַל כֵּן בָּאָה עָלָיו בּוּשָׁה

analysis_notes.critical_note: Torah #235 is entirely absent from torahData.js. The reference field skips from 234 to 239 with no 235 entry. All 9 concepts identified above need to be added as new bechina edges to the dataset. The minimum required edges are: (1) יום טוב — רגל, (2) יום טוב — מועד, (3) שחוק — שמחות נפולות, (4) עבודת אלילים — בשת, (5) עבודת אלילים — בזיון מועדות.
analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror_structure: Package 1 (good: יום טוב/רגל/מועד = the holy festival vessel) mirrors Package 3 (evil: בזיון מועדות/עבודת אלילים/בשת = the desecration of that same vessel). The same concept — מועד — appears as the holy festival in Package 1 and as the object of disgrace (בזיון מועדות) in Package 3. This is the classic shared-node polarity fracture point described in framework.md.
analysis_notes.eitza_connections_noted: The Torah's causal chain (eitza, not bechina): פגם שמחת יום טוב → רגל מועד/נפילה → שחוק העולם → בושה. And separately: בזיון מועדות → כפרה OR זכרון לתשובה. These are eitza flows between packages, not bechina connections within packages.
